g.text: Measured against an average-gray pixel, background pixels supplied 79% of the old model's
evidence for "bolt"; after retraining, 66%, and the gray-bench errors were gone
This book's simulation (figures/scripts/ch17_experiments.py; data/ch17_occlusion*.csv): constructed 12 x 12 images, not Sam's real photos. Darker = the pixel pushed harder
toward "bolt" (one-pixel occlusion against a fixed average-gray pixel, change in log-odds). Outlined squares = the bolt's pixels. For this glass-box model the map
matched the exact contributions (correlation 1.00 and 0.99). Against other baselines the old model's share runs from 13.5% to 84% (data/ch17_baseline_sensitivity.csv).
